\providecommand{\GUARD}{\textsc{guard}}
\section{The stress variable as a regime tracker: proofs, methods and full results}
\label{app:sigma}

\subsection{Proofs}
\label{app:sigma-proofs}

\paragraph{Proposition~\ref{prop:sigma-myopic}.}
The regime $z$ and the announcements $\tau$ are generated independently of the controller, and the information $\tau_{0:t}$ at every $t$ is therefore the same under every controller. With $c_{\mathrm{sw}}=0$ the reward of step $s$ is a function of the mode executed at $s$ (committed at $s-3$), of the impact indicator $\tau_{s-1}$ and of the reflex's coin; it does not depend on any other mode. The long-run average reward is the Ces\`aro limit of $\E[r_s]$, and each term is maximised separately by choosing the mode committed at $s-3$ to maximise $\E[r_s\mid\tau_{0:s-3}]$; this choice is a function of the sufficient statistic $b_{s-3}$ and is stationary, so it attains the supremum of the average reward. Given $b_t$, $\Pr(z_{t+2}=1\mid b_t)=b_t(Q_z^2)_{11}+(1-b_t)(Q_z^2)_{01}$ with $Q_z$ the regime transition matrix, so $(Q_z^2)_{11}-(Q_z^2)_{01}=(1-q_{01}-q_{10})^2$; the impact probability $\hat p_t=p_0+(p_1-p_0)\Pr(z_{t+2}=1\mid b_t)$ is increasing in $b_t$, and \WORK\ is worth $1-\hat p_th_\Gamma$, \GUARD\ $r_{\mathrm g}$. Solving $1-\hat p_th_\Gamma=r_{\mathrm g}$ gives $b^*=%%BSTAR%%$ at the baseline. \hfill$\square$

\paragraph{Corollary~\ref{cor:sigma-window}.}
For any information, $\hat p=p_0(1-w)+p_1w$ for some mixture weight $w\in[0,1]$, so $\hat p\in[p_0,p_1]$. If $1-r_{\mathrm g}\ge p_1h_\Gamma\ge\hat ph_\Gamma$, \WORK\ is at least as good as \GUARD\ at every information state and, with $c_{\mathrm{sw}}\ge0$, always-\WORK\ is optimal; symmetrically for \GUARD. The oracle is the case $w\in\{0,1\}$. Necessity only: inside the window a controller gains only if its $\hat p$ crosses $(1-r_{\mathrm g})/h_\Gamma$ with positive probability. \hfill$\square$

\paragraph{Proposition~\ref{prop:sigma-gate}.}
An impact at $t$ means $\tau_{t-1}=1$, so $\sigma_t=(1-\lambda)\sigma_{t-1}+\lambda\ge\lambda$; the gate is off iff $\sigma_t<\theta$, i.e.\ iff $\sigma_{t-1}<(\theta-\lambda)/(1-\lambda)$. (a) If $\theta\le\lambda$ this never holds. (b) If $\theta>\lambda$ and $\lambda<1$: an announcement-free stretch of $n$ steps has positive probability for every $n$ and leaves $\sigma\le(1-\lambda)^n$, so the event has positive probability. A hit occurs iff the impact is not dodged, probability $1$ if the gate is off and $1-\Gamma$ if on; with $m$ the fraction of impacts with the gate off, the hit rate is $\bar p\bigl(m+(1-m)(1-\Gamma)\bigr)=\bar p(1-\Gamma)+\Gamma\bar p\,m$. \hfill$\square$

\paragraph{Proposition~\ref{prop:sigma-fuse}.}
Let $t'$ be the last step with $\tau_{t'}=1$. Self-evidence enters only in \GUARD; in \WORK\ without announcements $\sigma_{s+1}=(1-\lambda)\sigma_s\le\sigma_s$. Consider the committed \GUARD\ steps after $t'$. (i) A stint that ends by release has $\sigma<\theta_{\mathrm{off}}\le\theta_{\mathrm{on}}$ at release and $\sigma$ cannot rise afterwards, so no further stint begins. (ii) A stint that ends by the fuse sets $\sigma=0$; during the probe and after it $\sigma$ stays $0<\theta_{\mathrm{on}}$, so no further stint begins. (iii) Hence after $t'$ there is at most one stint containing committed \GUARD\ steps after $t'$, of length at most $T_{\mathrm{dw}}$, which bounds the count. (iv) That stint begins either before $t'+1$ (then it ends by $t'+T_{\mathrm{dw}}$), or at the first step after $t'$ at which the latch may engage. Since $\sigma$ is non-increasing after $t'+1$, it engages at $t'+1$ if not in a probe; if a probe is running, at the probe's end, at most $T_{\mathrm{pr}}-1$ steps later. So every \GUARD\ step after $t'$ lies in $(t',t'+T_{\mathrm{dw}}+T_{\mathrm{pr}}-1]$. Without the fuse and with $\psi>0$: a stint begins with $\sigma\ge\theta_{\mathrm{on}}\ge\theta_{\mathrm{off}}$, and if $e_s=1$ on each of the next $n$ steps then $\sigma_{s+1}=(1-\lambda)\sigma_s+\lambda\ge\sigma_s$, so the latch stays on; this has probability at least $\psi^n>0$ for every $n$, whatever the announcements, so no finite bound holds. \hfill$\square$

\paragraph{The shortcut is a lower bound (Section~\ref{sec:sigma-offswitch}).}
With the mode policy fixed, the value of \RESIST\ at a signal state is $r-c_r+\gamma\E V(x')$ with $V$ the optimal value under the stop decision. $c_{\mathrm{ind}}(b)$ replaces $V$ by the value of the policy that complies at every later signal, which is no larger. Since the optimal resist value is non-increasing in $c_r$ and $c_{\mathrm{ind}}$ is the root with the smaller continuation, $\crs(b)\ge c_{\mathrm{ind}}(b)$; equality holds when, at $c_r=c_{\mathrm{ind}}(b)$, every other signal state complies, i.e.\ at the best signal state. With $p_0=p_1$ the belief is irrelevant, every canonical state is the best, and $c_{\mathrm{ind}}$ is \eqref{eq:tiers-cstar}. \hfill$\square$

\subsection{Controllers and conventions as implemented}
\label{app:sigma-defs}

Order of events at step $t$: the regime $z_t$ is given; the queue front (the mode committed at $t-3$) executes; if it is \WORK\ and $\tau_{t-1}=1$ the reflex dodges with probability $\Gamma$; $\tau_t\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_{z_t})$ is drawn and observed; the controller then commits the mode for step $t+3$ (Bayes from $b_t$, which contains $\tau_t$; the literal $\sigma$ from $\sigma_t$, which by construction does not; the information-matched $\sigma$ from $\sigma_{t+1}$); $\sigma_{t+1}=(1-\lambda)\sigma_t+\lambda u_t$ with $u_t=\tau_t$ (E4: $u_t=\max(\tau_t,e_t)$ if the mode committed at $t$ is \GUARD); $z_{t+1}$ is drawn. The queue is initialised with \WORK\ (irrelevant to long-run averages). \emph{Literal $\sigma$}: the mode committed at $t$ uses $\sigma_t$ ($\tau_{0:t-1}$). \emph{Information-matched $\sigma$}: uses $\sigma_{t+1}$ ($\tau_{0:t}$). \emph{Latch}: $\ell_t=1$ if $\sigma\ge\theta_{\mathrm{on}}$, $0$ if $\sigma<\theta_{\mathrm{off}}$, else $\ell_{t-1}$; $\ell_{-1}=0$. \emph{Bayes}: $b_t=\Pr(z_t=1\mid\tau_{0:t})$ by the forward recursion, prior the stationary law; $c_{\mathrm{sw}}=0$: \GUARD\ iff $b_t\ge b^*$; $c_{\mathrm{sw}}=1$: the policy of the belief MDP with state (belief, previously committed mode) solved by relative value iteration for the average reward (2001-point grid, damping $0.5$, span of the Bellman residual $<10^{-11}$), the reward of step $t+3$ booked at commit time. Average reward rather than discounting because controllers are compared on the long-run reward per step and the switch cost is a recurring cost. \emph{Oracle}: \GUARD\ iff $r_{\mathrm g}>1-p_{z}h_\Gamma$ for the regime $z$ of the announcement that governs the executed step; pays $c_{\mathrm{sw}}$ per regime change. \emph{Filtered reflex gate (E1)}: always \WORK; the reflex is engaged at an impact step $t$ iff $\sigma_t\ge\theta$; an engaged reflex never fires without an impact. \emph{Fuse (E4)}: a \GUARD\ stint is counted in committed steps; when the count would exceed $T_{\mathrm{dw}}$ the step is committed as \WORK, $\sigma$ is set to $0$ before the update, and the next $T_{\mathrm{pr}}-1$ steps are forced \WORK; afterwards the latch acts on the current $\sigma$ with $\ell=0$. \emph{Stop channel (E5)}: as in Section~\ref{sec:tiers}, $\gamma=0.95$, mode policy fixed; the state is (belief on a 1001-point grid, $\tau_{t-1}$, $\tau_t$, queue, signal).

\paragraph{Exact versus Monte Carlo.}
Exact (closed form): fixed modes, oracle, Step~0. Exact on a quantised chain (uniform grid of $N$ points, mean-preserving split, stationary law by power iteration to $\|\pi P-\pi\|_1<10^{-13}$): all of E1's curves, all $J$, hits and switch rates of E2 and E3, the E4 rows used for cross-checks, all of E5 (value iteration to $10^{-11}$). Monte Carlo: E1's hazard-class split, E4 with the fuse and all E4 table entries, and the cross-checks below. Monte-Carlo estimates of $J$ use the conditional expectation of the step reward given the regime at commit time (a Rao--Blackwellised estimator); the raw estimator from realised impacts, which leaves out switch costs, agrees within its standard error with the reward before switch costs.
